//: SPEC 29.2/29.7: inject MDV highlighting into fenced blocks whose info string
starts with `mdv`, inside ordinary Markdown documents.
`injectionSelector` targets the fenced-code scope rather than the whole
Markdown scope, so this grammar is only consulted where it can possibly
match — a `.md` file with no mdv fence pays nothing for having the extension
The block body is delegated to `text.html.markdown.mdv`'s own repository so
there is exactly one definition of the header/separator/data structure. A
`-text.html.markdown.mdv` is load-bearing. Scope selectors match by dotted
prefix, so a bare `text.html.markdown` selector would also match inside an
.mdv file — whose own grammar already handles the block — and the two would
compete for the same fence. Excluding our own scope keeps the injection to
the case it exists for: `mdv` fences inside ordinary `.md` files.
